facts.title: China rejects calls for ‘pacing’ on AI development, fearing it would entrench US tech lead
facts.summary: Calls by US tech leaders for a voluntary slowdown in artificial intelligence development have run into sharp pushback from Chinese researchers and state media, who question whether the proposal is a genuine push for responsibility or an effort to entrench America’s technological lead. The debate intensified on Monday when OpenAI CEO Sam Altman joined a growing chorus of Silicon Valley leaders demanding industry-wide “pacing”, warning that competitive pressure must not override safety as AI...
facts.article_excerpt: Chinese researchers say a slowdown would protect established US incumbents while freezing latecomers out of the market 3 -MIN READ 3 -MIN 11 Listen Chong Ming Lee Published: 6:00pm, 14 Sep 2026 Calls by US tech leaders for a voluntary slowdown in artificial intelligence development have run into sharp pushback from Chinese researchers and state media, who question whether the proposal is a genuine push for responsibility or an effort to entrench America’s technological lead. The debate intensified on Monday when OpenAI CEO Sam Altman joined a growing chorus of Silicon Valley leaders demanding industry-wide “pacing”, warning that competitive pressure must not override safety as AI advanced rapidly. “The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened,” Altman wrote on social media platform X. “Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot.”

draft.headline: China rejects Silicon Valley's call to slow AI down
draft.caption:
China has pushed back on calls from US tech leaders to slow down AI development. 🇨🇳🤖

On Monday, OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman joined other Silicon Valley leaders asking the industry to agree on "pacing", meaning a voluntary slowdown. He said competitive pressure must not override safety.

"The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened," Altman wrote on X.

Chinese researchers and state media are not buying it. Their argument is that a slowdown would protect the companies already out in front, and freeze the ones arriving late out of the market.

What cannot be settled from the outside is which motive is the real one. This report is recent, and the two sides are describing the exact same proposal in opposite terms.

Altman's side says safety is the first thing that gets cut when everyone is racing; the Chinese researchers say a pause written by the leader is just the leader keeping the lead. Which reading do you land on? 🤔

Source: SCMP

美國科技圈在喊 AI 要一起放慢腳步,中國那邊回得很直接:這不是為了安全,是為了把現在的領先位置鎖起來。

#AI競賽
喊的人裡面有 OpenAI 的 Sam Altman。他週一在 X 上說,競爭壓力不能蓋過安全,世界應該要能相信,開發出越來越強 AI 的美國公司會負責任地行事,尤其是在進展的斜率還在變陡的時候。他們用的詞叫 pacing,意思是整個產業講好一起踩煞車。
中國研究者的反駁不是喊口號,是一條市場邏輯:現在踩煞車,已經跑在前面的公司位置就固定下來,後面才起步的等於被關在門外。官媒跟著問的是,這到底是真心想負責任,還是想把美國的技術領先直接寫進規則裡。

同一個提案,兩種讀法。Altman 那邊說,大家都在衝的時候,第一個被犧牲的往往就是安全;中國研究者那邊說,由領先者提出的暫停,本質上就是領先者保住領先。你站哪一邊?

facts.title: Driver who killed Team GB triathlete to be deported
facts.summary: Romanian van driver Visile Barbu's appeal against deportation was dismissed by a judge.
facts.article_excerpt: Image source, Family photo Image caption, Rebecca Comins' family said they are so proud of what she achieved in her life A Romanian van driver jailed for killing a Team GB triathlete by driving into the back of her bike has lost an appeal against being deported. Visile Barbu, 50 was delivering furniture to a driver in Calais when he hit Rebecca Comins' bike in June 2022. Barbu drove straight into the back of Comins rather than move into an empty lane of the dual carriageway. He was was found guilty of causing her death by dangerous driving following a five day trial . At the hearing in Newport, immigration judge Ian Boyes said: The nature of the offending is important. This was not an accident. It was not a slight misjudgement. It was committed using a vehicle which should not have been on the road. Image caption, Vasile Barbu told police during interview that he could not explain how he hit Rebecca Comins Comins, 52, was nine minutes into a cycling time trial on the A40 near Raglan, Monmouthshire, when Barbu tried to overtake. He said he had seen her, but did not know why he hit her, claiming he would ask himself the question for his whole life . When his van was examined following the crash it was found to be unfit for the road and its load overweight which would have increased the emergency breaking distances and ability to turn the wheel, according to a vehicle examiner. Barbu moved to Britain in 2002 to become a pub chef at Old Pandy public house and eventually owned the pub. Barbu married a Romanian woman, Maria, in 2004 and had twins, who are now adults. He filed an appeal to stop him from being deported, and said it would be unduly harsh for both him and his family to relocate permanently to Romania, where he said he has no home or source of income. He said he identified closely with British culture and traditions and regarded the UK as his permanent home. His wife Maria said she would not relocate to Romania, and would be unable to cope without her husband. On 7 September, Boyes said as Barbu's children were adults and do not depend on him, it would not be unduly harsh to remove him. He said the very significant public interest in deportation outweighs the appellant's private and family life considerations.

draft.headline: Driver who killed triathlete loses appeal against deportation
draft.caption:
A van driver who killed a Team GB triathlete has lost his appeal against being deported from Britain. ⚖️

Rebecca Comins, 52, was nine minutes into a cycling time trial on a dual carriageway near Raglan in Monmouthshire in June 2022 when Vasile Barbu drove into the back of her bike. There was an empty lane he could have moved into. His van was later found to be unfit for the road and carrying an overweight load, which a vehicle examiner said would have increased its emergency braking distance.

"This was not an accident. It was not a slight misjudgement. It was committed using a vehicle which should not have been on the road."

Barbu, 50, moved to Britain in 2002 to work as a pub chef and eventually owned the pub. He married in 2004 and has twins who are now adults. He argued that being sent to Romania, where he says he has no home and no income, would be unduly harsh on him and his family, and his wife said she would not move there and could not cope without him.

He told police he had seen Comins but did not know why he hit her, and said he would ask himself that question for his whole life. On 7 September the judge dismissed the appeal, saying the children are adults and do not depend on him.

The judge says the public interest in deportation outweighs the life Barbu built in Britain; Barbu says Britain has been his permanent home since 2002 and his wife will not follow him to Romania. Where do you land on that? 💬

2022 年 6 月,52 歲的 Rebecca Comins 在雙線道上跑自行車計時賽,騎了九分鐘,50 歲的 Vasile Barbu 想超車,直接從後面撞上她。旁邊明明有一條空的車道。事後檢查那台車根本不能上路,而且超載。

撞死英國三鐵國手的羅馬尼亞籍廂型車司機上訴失敗,移民法官決定把他遣返回羅馬尼亞。案發當下,他旁邊就有一條空的車道,他還是直直撞了上去。

#英國遣返
細節是這樣:2022 年 6 月,52 歲的 Rebecca Comins 在 Monmouthshire 一段雙線道上跑計時賽,騎了九分鐘。50 歲的 Vasile Barbu 想超車,從後面撞上她的腳踏車。他跟警方說他有看到她,但講不出為什麼會撞上去,只說這個問題他會問自己一輩子。事後檢查那台車:不能上路,而且超載,煞車距離會變長,方向盤也比較難轉。
他不是剛到英國的人。2002 年來英國在一間酒吧當廚師,後來整間店變成他的;2004 年結婚,雙胞胎現在都成年了。他說回羅馬尼亞沒有房子也沒有收入,英國才是他永久的家。他太太說她不會搬過去,也沒辦法一個人撐。

移民法官 9 月 7 日的理由很直接:小孩都成年、不依賴他,所以把他遣返不算「過度嚴苛」,遣返的公共利益比他的家庭生活更重。法官那邊說,留下他等於讓公共利益退讓;他那邊說,他 2002 年就來了,家也在這裡,不該被整個拔掉。你覺得這種案子該往哪邊判?
